en.name: AGRecorder
en.short_description: High-framerate screen recorder with dual-channel system + mic audio
en.subtitle: Voice recorder with location
en.description:
AGRecorder is a voice recorder that remembers where you were.

RECORD
One button. Start, stop, done. Audio is captured as AAC and written straight to your device.

LOCATION
Each recording can carry the coordinates it was made at. AGRecorder asks the device for GPS first; if that is unavailable it falls back to an approximate lookup, and it always tells you which of the two produced the fix rather than presenting a guess as a reading.

PERMISSIONS, PLAINLY
Microphone access is what makes the app work. Location is used only to tag a recording, and only if you let it. Nothing is uploaded on your behalf.

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing AGRecorder.

AGRecorder is a one-screen audio recorder. No account, no sign-in, no purchase, no onboarding. The microphone is the only permission it ever requests, and the app works with the radio off.

Three things that look like defects but are not, so you do not have to guess:
• The "Camera" chip beside "Microphone" changes nothing. RecordBackend.start() in lib/platform/record_backend.dart ignores the selected source and always records audio. There is no video capture in this build and the listing does not claim any.
• The badge reading "Cloud Storage Sync: Connected" and the button reading "Stop & Sync to Cloud" are labels carried over from the desktop app this was ported from. There is no cloud, no account and no upload — the app issues no network request from any screen. Stopping simply finalises the file on the device.
• Info.plist declares NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription, but this build never asks for location: the GPS helper in lib/domain/gps.dart is not referenced by the UI. No location prompt will appear during review, and no coordinates are read or stored.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app. It opens straight onto the recorder.
2. Tap "Start Recording" and allow the microphone prompt. The panel changes to "Recording…".
3. Tap "Stop & Sync to Cloud". The take is written to the app's own Documents directory as agrecorder_<timestamp>.m4a (AAC-LC), and the filename appears under the panel as "Saved: …". Nothing leaves the device.
4. To see the denial path, turn microphone access off for the app in iOS Settings and tap Start again. The app shows "Permission denied. Enable microphone access in Settings." and remains usable.
5. Tap the globe icon in the header to change the interface language.
6. Put the device in airplane mode and repeat steps 2–3. Everything still works, which is the point.

Privacy:
• Data collected: Nothing about you. No account, no profile, no identifiers.
• Microphone: Required, and used only while a recording is running.
• Recordings: Kept in the app's Documents directory on the device. There is no upload code path.
• Network: None. No screen in the app makes a network request.
• Location: Not requested and not used in this build.
• Tracking: None. Crash reporting is Firebase Crashlytics only; there is no advertising or analytics SDK, and the advertising identifier is never read, so no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
